note: Belarus: Russians move freely; nationals of the countries listed enter without a visa for 90 or 30 days, and under a temporary regime to 31 December 2026 the EU, EFTA, the UK and the European microstates for 30 days; nationals of the e-Visa list apply online (30 days), the conditional e-Visa nationalities only with a Schengen, Cypriot or Irish visa (not modelled). Everyone else needs a visa. Read from Wikipedia's copy. Checked on 2026-11-03 against the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' own pages (Common Crawl captures of September and October 2026): they confirmed Russia, the 90- and 30-day lists and the European regime to 31 December 2026, which gives Poland, Lithuania and Latvia 90 days, not 30, so those three were moved to 90 days. The Ministry lists the CIS neighbours and Ecuador visa-free with no period, so their stays stand on Wikipedia's copy; it names only some of the 68 e-Visa countries (30 days), and the 30-day entry through six airports for 76 countries isn't modelled.

sources.title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Belarus, Visa-free entry for citizens of a number of European countries — Common Crawl CC-MAIN-2026-43 capture of 2026-10-07
sources.said: Citizens of 38 European states are eligible to enter Belarus without a visa via all international road and rail border crossing points ... may remain in Belarus for up to 30 days from the date of entry. For citizens of Poland, Lithuania and Latvia (including holders of Latvia’s non-citizen status), the permitted stay is extended to 90 days from the date of entry. [list of 38] ... Travellers may make use of this visa-free regime an unlimited number of times until December 31, 2026 inclusive. The total duration of visa-free stays must not exceed 90 days within a calendar year.
